[quote=the_crystalline_empire;61653374][b]August 7, 2028: Briefing[/b]

Haakon Strømm had spent the night up on the telephone with Begren, who had travelled to Thýven to personally oversee the recentralisation of forces there as well as to arrest and crack down on the local secessionists, so far Begren had assured him that he was successful with the duc of Thýven in state custody.

Things are not going so well in the East, intoned Haakon over the phone as he looked at a map of Rosenmarkke, The Sallach forces are sweeping from the north, and our own forces are apparently caught up in a skirmish snear the Mittlemarkke and Belgarde border, apparently supporters of the movement, he continued with a frown.

I have received word from the SCSID office there that Antoine plans on surrendering, replied Begren, I shall make an attempt to travel into the region to personally ensure the situation does not occur, but, I cannot assure that I will be able to do that too son, 

Why the hell not? demanded Haakon.

Because, the situation in Thýven still remains volatile, especially amongst the citizens of the regions which we annexed in January, the local puppet governments there have been overthrown, replied Begren.

Has any effort been made to retake Knygta and Deyn? asked Haakon.

Sir, you know full well that we were going to hold off on that, replied Begren, The islands can be isolated, 

They have attempted to join Montfleur, apparently, replied Haakon.

I am aware, 

But Montfleur has given no reply, which means they intend to play games with us, continued Haakon.

Of course, replied Begren, Anything else? 

No, our forces will be in Belgarde within the day, I see no issues at hand, replied Strømm hanging up the phone, and staring out the window into the capital city.[/quote]
[quote=sallach;61654525][b]Battle of Belgarde[/b]

The region of South Belgarde is now in the twilight of its existence. The Count of Porcéan, the self-proclaimed Regent of La Rosemarche, was now on track to seizing nearly half the region;s territory. The "Gardens" surrounding Wavre, with its strategically critical network of hedges, tunnels, ad hoc fortifications, and hillscapes were now completely in Sallacher control. Soviet forces had surrendered in droves, their arms safely stocked away on piles for imminent transfer to pro-Sallacher militias. All that was left now was to win.

Porcéan, from his forward operating base at "Hotel Carlodun" north of the western Belgardian airbase, was now left with his advisors to plan out the proper course of action to see the total de-communization of Belgarde and, with holy fortuity, the rest of the country. 

According to scouting patrols, Wavre had been heavily barricaded by citizens' militias seemingly hell-bent on preserving their red revolution. Of these barricades, the patrols noted that militia armaments were "largely unspectacular", limited to small arms and vehicles seized from the local armory and barracks of the city. However, Porcéan was nevertheles advised to exercise caution, with scouts remaining certain that militia forces possessed some manner of explosives capable of disabling or even destroying the Palatine Guard's Char 15 tanks.

To help bolster any attempts to breakthrough to the capital, Porcéan would decide to form a new military force in Belgarde constituted by pro-Sallacher forces and gunmen who were willing to fight in exchange for promises of pensions after the war.

The battalion-sized Corps de Maréchaussée would be formed under senatorial proclamation and placed under Sallacher command with an overall manpower of 1,405 men. Porcéan's lieutenant, Hugo de lAuxerrois, would be placed in charge of the Marechaussees for the duration of the campaign, granting its members total sanction to act as a police unit and local military force in occupied Belgarde. Due to budget limitations, the Marechaussees would be mostly clad in the same gear worn by previous soviet forces, if they had gear, and would be only distinguisable from local Rosenmarkket troops by the use of a yellow armband on their right arm.

Together with the initial Sallacher forces, the combined invasion force now sat at almost 8,000 men, and would for a time be the most effective fighting force in the eastern Rose Marches.

On sighting Wavre, the Count of Porcéan would set in motion a series of operations to rapidly overwhelm the city's militia. The Palatine Tank Company would spearhead the initial assault with its ten Char 15 tanks and a dozen AMC 88 APCs, their advance screened by a ferocious barrage of 155 mm howitzers and several companies of Palatines and Maréchaussées. Several [i]Abeille-4[/i] one-way attack drones would also be deployed by Sallacher forces to forcibly dislodge militia forces from the barricades and to destroy any key weapons stockpiles to deplete Wavre's ability to resist the inevitable.[/quote]

[b]On the Open Road[/b]

Iseg Radwell and his men found themselves grouped together with an infantry and tank unit from the central command, having been ordered to join them on their march towards the city of Wavre. The situation there was apparently dire and should the city fall Rosenmarkke itself would fall. At least, thats what the propagandist had said during her speech to rally the troops. 

However, most of Radwells men had called bull, in private of course, and had determined to confront the head of the unit, a tired old colonel named Rudolf Anslemjner. However, the time had not yet arrived as the forces were ordered to travel on foot to Belgarde to save resources.

Thus as the soldiers rode and walked along the long highway which led to the border of Belgarde, the summer sun beating down upon their backs, Radwell decided to strike up conversation with a young lieutenant who had been riding with him in the convoy truck.

Where are you from? he asked the soldier, who couldnt be more than 23. 

Westmarkke, sir, replied the lietuenant.

Nice region, they are known for their plums no? asked Radwell.

Yes sir, my father grows them in fact, smiled the lieutenant, unsure why the captain was speaking to him. 

Radwell smiled, I visited the region last summer actually, at the beach, 

Did you? Which one? asked the lieutenant.

Radovka? intoned Radwell, thinking for a moment.

Yes I believe you northerners spell it with a j instead of a k, replied the lieutenant.

Ah, yes, of course, clapped Radwell with a chuckle.

When do you think this war will end? asked the lieutenant.

It will end, when either we are taken over, or, when we declare victory, replied Radwell.

Do you think we will win? asked the lieutenant.

Radwell gave no reply, merely staring down the road, that reply was enough for the young lieutenant.

[b]Advance[/b]

It had been a troubling day for the members of the palace staff in Montfleur, Henri had been itching to leap to arms and traverse into Belgarde with the Gendarme, however, Eleonore, having had to calm him down and remind him that the situation was still not fully secure, forced the king to address a new issue which had arisen.

The parties of the assembly had delivered an ultimatum to the palace the day before, at an ungodly hour of the night, Eleonore had quietly kept the ultimatum away for the morning, producing it while the king read in his study.

They want me to end the war? asked Henri, putting the piece of paper down.

Yes, they are threatening a war powers vote, replied Eleonore.

They do not have the votes, smirked Henri, handing her the paper, They will not pass it,

I have spoken with the right union, replied Eleonore, Theyd back it, apparently the left and centre offered a sweet package on school choice and regional decentralisation, 

Henri scoffed, We are at war, about to take in an entire nation, and they are worried about regional decentralisation?! 

Eleonore shrugged, Whatever keeps them distracted,

Henri tilted his head, I have never understood them, we are winning in Belgarde, the city will fall on August the 10th, and after them, the rest of the regions will follow, these parties have nothing to be worried about, he waved his hand.

So what is your message? asked Eleonore.

Let them eat fried chicken, chuckled Henri.

Eleonore gave a sigh, and walked out of the room. 

[b]The Embattled Citizens[/b]

Word had reached the city of Wavre that the Sallach forces and Montfleurois forces were nearly 10 km away from the city. Having received little to no pushback from the police, thousands of citizens, hopping in vehicles and bikes and other transportation would leave the city to greet the Sallach forces.

In the meantime, following an order by Antoine, the police finally engaged with the barricades, attempting to ram them down, with several successfully collapsing and killing 7 people. Enraged, the citizens of Wavre began firefights in the street with the police. Gunfire broke out along the streets.

Nearly 5,000 of the 40,000 population had left the city up till then, however, upon the breakout of further violence another 5,000 were estimated to have begun to leave en masse, heading for Mittlemarkke and other parts of Rosenmarkke.

[spoiler=Citharo Line, in Minhokae]

[b]A Pleasant Morning[/b]

6 July

Liang Hao sat in his study, reading his newspaper. He preferred to read news the "old-fashioned" way, though he didn't think it was old fashioned at all. For him, it was just a normal task of his that he did everyday. Every morning, he went out on his porch with a cup of coffee in hand, waiting for the paperboy to come and drop off the news of the day. Pingyao, a Qianxun minority village, was the home of many Qianxun politicians in Minhokae.

"Shūshu (Uncle) Liang! Good morning!" the paperboy said, handing the newspaper to him.

"Xiǎo (Little) Cheng!" "How are you?" responded Liang.

"Ah, still the same old. How are you, Shūshu?"

"I have a new project today. I'm going to be requesting permission to found a new political party for us Qianxun in Minhokae."

"Best of luck Shūshu!" the boy said, too young to understand what it meant.

"Thank you, run along now, háizi (child)."

The paperboy waved and ran to the next house.

[b]Request to the King[/b]

The night before had been spent meeting with friends of his, with prominent ties to all of Qianxun's socialist parties. On a base of mutually agreed principles, they agreed to adopting new socialism and civil-military fusion as key party ideologies. In addition to this, they adopted the Amore, pace e felicità philosophy by Argo Lo Pilato as a core philosophy of the party, seen in Volume 2 of the Acta Publica of the Socialist International.

Today, Liang Hao would write to the King in the presence of his friends, who would sign the letter once it was finished along with him. It read:

"May it please Your Majesty,

I wish to inform you of an important occurrence that deserves your attention. Today, on 6 July, 2028, here in Jīngjī Province, my friends and I have decided to form a political party for the Qianxun minority here in Minhokae, the Qianxun Minority Party. You may find that we are all people who have ties to all of the socialist parties in Qianxun, and are well-known in our places of residence here in Minhokae to advocate the legal recognition for this movement, and we hope soon-to-be political party, should Your Majesty accept our request.

Attached you will find the list of ideologies and the philosophy of our movement. We hope that Your Majesty will view this in a positive light as a bridge connecting Minhokaen and Qianxun people in the greater struggle for equality for all.

We have the honor to remain, Sir, Your Majesty's most humble and obedient servants.

Sincerely,

Liang Hao, Li Jun, Huang Wei, Zhou Long, Lin Zihao, Su Jinhai, Fu Lijun"

[b]The King's Approval Granted[/b]

The King had fought hard for cooperation with Qianxun, as seen after successful negotiation to introduce the Minhokae-Qianxun Chamber of Commerce, which already boasted positive effects for the economies of both nations. Now, in a bid to introduce greater cooperation with Qianxun and the Socialist International, the King decided to approve the party request of the Qianxun Minority Party, with it being a duty of his, as he was seen as the unbiased leader and decision-maker of the country, a choice that the Prime Minister or Parliament couldn't make due to bias.

After approving the political party in a formal letter granting permission for the political party to be founded and sending notice to the National Election Commission, the King, having seen this as the perfect moment to boost cooperation with Qianxun, called the Prime Minister and informed him of his decision. The King let him know that he had invited Qianxun and Socialist International military officials to Minhokae for secret military cooperation talks, aimed at protecting the interests of Minhokae and that of Qianxun and the Socialist International from Daesun's expansionist agenda. The topics of training bases, not formal military bases (to preserve neutrality) and nuclear energy cooperation were mentioned.

[b]En Route to Boseong-gun[/b]

After picking up the Qianxun and Sanguinian military officials who arrived in Minhokae via a commercial flight to hide their identities, from the designated location in an unmarked, though still protected vehicle, the officials and the driver arrived at Boseong-gun, a village in the southwest area of Minhokae. 

There, in an old house completely secluded house from the rest of the village population, in the middle of a green tea field, the King, the Director of the National Intelligence Service, the Prime Minister, and the Chiefs of Staff of the Army, Navy, and Air Force, as well as the Commandant of the Marine Corps, subordinate to the Chief of Staff of the Navy, all walked out of the door of the house and stood outside of it. They would all bow as a sign of respect to the newly-arrived officials, except for the King due to his rank, who would walk over to shake their hands. [/spoiler]
